festivals: Vaikunta Ekadashi - 21-day festival in Margazhi (December-January); the grandest celebration, attracting about 1 million visitors

history.dynasty: Early Cholas (Dharmavarcholan and Killivalavan - foundations); contributions of the Alwars; later Pandyas, Hoysalas and the Vijayanagara Empire (Krishnadevaraya, Achyuta Deva Raya)
history.period: Foundations in early Chola antiquity; growth over centuries through medieval dynasties; the Rajagopuram completed 1987
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: this temple is NOT in Tiruchirappalli town - it is in SRIRANGAM town, on Srirangam island between the Kaveri and Kollidam rivers (~9-10 km from Tiruchirappalli Junction). Documented with the corrected town. The Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple, Srirangam is the largest temple complex in India and is listed by UNESCO as the biggest functioning Hindu temple in the world (156 acres / 631,000 sq m, perimeter ~4.1 km; the still-larger Angkor Wat no longer holds worship). It is counted the FIRST of the 108 Divya Desams dedicated to Vishnu and one of the self-manifested Svayam Vyakta Kshetras; it is glorified in the Thiviya Pirabandham of the Alwar saints (6th-9th c.). Legend: Rama gave the reclining Vishnu idol to Vibhishana, who set it down on the Kaveri bank; it refused to move, facing south toward Lanka. The complex has seven concentric prakarams (walled enclosures) and 21 gopurams, with the southern Rajagopuram at 237-239.5 ft the tallest temple tower in Asia - begun under Achyuta Deva Raya, stalled 400+ years, completed in 8 years and consecrated 25 March 1987 by the 44th jeeyar of Ahobila Matha. There is a gold-plated gopuram, and Ramanuja (11th c.) made his monastic home here and wrote his Brahma Sutra commentaries (his preserved body is enshrined in the temple). The temple follows the Thenkalai tradition of worship (Pancharatra Agama). It is the same Ranganatha of the Vibhishana legend linked to 948 (Ucchi Pillayar, Rockfort).

name: Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple
town: Srirangam (CSV town 'Tiruchirappalli' is WRONG - the temple is in Srirangam town, ~9-10 km from Tiruchirappalli Junction)
town_description: Srirangam is a temple town on Srirangam Island - 31 km long, 2.4 km wide - formed by the Kaveri to the south and its distributary the Kollidam to the north. It is part of the Tiruchirappalli Municipal Corporation (Srirangam zone), is home to a large Sri Vaishnava population, and has a thriving pilgrim economy with frequent city buses (route 1) linking it to Trichy.
tradition: Hinduism (Vaishnavism - Sri Vaishnavism, Thenkalai; Pancharatra Agama)

travel.railway: Srirangam station (~1 km); Tiruchirappalli Junction - about 9-10 km.
travel.road: City bus route 1 from Tiruchirappalli Central Bus Stand every 5 minutes, round the clock; autorickshaws and tourist taxis available.

visitor_information.best_time: November to February (20-30°C); Vaikunta Ekadashi (December-January) is the peak festival with extreme crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Published on the official HR&CE portal: 6:00 AM-9:00 PM with three ritual breaks when sanctum gates close - 7:15-9:00 AM, 12:30-2:15 PM, 5:30-7:00 PM (verify before visiting; festival days differ).
